source: Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — booklet 'ដំណាំពោត' (Corn Crop), Issue 1, 2003, funded by Asian Development Bank (ADB), Loan/Grant No. 1445-CAM(SF), section III (land preparation subsection)
text:
Plowing should be done thoroughly/finely so that soil moisture is retained for longer and plant roots can penetrate the soil easily. After plowing, the soil can be left to sun-dry (fallow) for about 5-15 days before planting.

For rainy-season cultivation, care must be taken to prevent waterlogging: drainage furrows should be dug every 1-2 rows within the field to drain off excess water. This also helps remove floating weeds (e.g., water lettuce/salvinia-type weeds), insect pests and worms, and helps prevent nutrient loss/leaching from the soil during the rainy season.
